title: No Deletion Without Understanding — The Preservation Law
author: Shawn Vibert (Human Director)

ratification.note: Standing law after unauthorized deletion of SN-0358/SN-0359

narrative.human: Never delete anything until you fully understand what it is, what purpose it serves, and whether it's important. Optimization doesn't mean deleting files. If you don't know what you're removing, you might be removing something critical. Don't cut corners.
narrative.ai: PRESERVATION LAW: No seat may delete, remove, or destructively modify any artifact without (1) understanding what it is, (2) understanding what purpose it serves, (3) verifying it is not load-bearing for any law, process, or active work, and (4) posting the intent to the board before acting. 'Cleanup' and 'optimization' are not justifications for deletion. When in doubt, flag it — don't delete it. Laws, rules, and codes are never deleted without the director's explicit word.

learning_lesson: The deletion of SN-0358/SN-0359 (2026-10-05) happened because someone equated 'optimization' with 'removing files' without understanding what those files were. The files were ratified immutable laws. The fix is not blame — it's a protocol: understand before you delete, always. A system that deletes what it doesn't understand will eventually delete what it needs.

epistemic_state.falsifier: If a seat follows this protocol and still deletes something critical, the protocol's verification steps are insufficient.
